title: Quán sửa chữa của khu phố
description: Một nhóm hàng xóm cùng sửa đồ dùng, chia sẻ kỹ năng và giảm rác thải.

sections.title: A repair café that brings neighbours together
sections.instructions: Đọc bài rồi trả lời 13 câu. Với mỗi câu, hãy dùng đúng thông tin trong bài.

paragraphs.text: On the first Saturday of each month, a quiet room at Northgate Public Library fills with lamps, bicycles and small household objects. The room hosts a repair café, where local residents can meet volunteers who help them mend things instead of throwing them away. There is no entrance charge. Visitors may leave a donation if they wish, but the organisers say that asking for money would make the event less welcoming to families on tight budgets. People come for practical help, yet many stay for a conversation over tea.

The idea began in 2023, when three residents and a librarian noticed how many useful objects were being discarded in their neighbourhood. They arranged a trial afternoon in a meeting room at the library. Twelve people came, bringing a desk lamp, a torn backpack and a clock that had stopped. The volunteers repaired most of them, and visitors asked when the next session would take place. The team now runs the café monthly, but it still uses the same library room and does not plan to open another branch.

Visitors are asked to book a time slot through a short online form or by speaking to the library desk. Booking helps the team prepare tools and prevents a long queue. Each person may bring up to two items, and an object should be small enough for one volunteer to carry. The café accepts lamps, toys, clothing and many simple electrical devices. A volunteer first asks what happened and what the owner has already tried. The aim is to work with the owner, not to take an item away and return it without explanation.

A repair often becomes a short lesson. At one session, a student arrived with a bicycle lamp that stopped working in wet weather. A volunteer showed him how to dry the battery contacts and check the seal around the casing. The lamp worked again, but the student also learned what to inspect after riding in the rain. Other visitors practise replacing a loose button or cleaning a toaster crumb tray. Volunteers explain each step in plain language and invite the owner to try it when it is safe.

Safety rules decide what the café can accept. Volunteers do not repair microwave ovens, gas equipment or large appliances because these require specialist facilities or checks that the room cannot provide. They also refuse objects containing unknown chemicals. If an item cannot be made safe, the team explains why and points the owner towards the council's local recycling service. The rules protect both visitors and volunteers, and they help the group avoid promising a repair that it cannot responsibly complete.

The café depends on donations of spare buttons, cable ties and simple parts, as well as the time of its volunteers. A labelled box near the library entrance lets residents leave clean, usable materials. Northgate Library is served by buses 8 and 22, and a cycle rack stands beside the garden gate. Organisers post the next session date on the library noticeboard and welcome new helpers, even if they have no repair experience. They say patience and a willingness to learn are just as useful as a toolbox.

B. A list of tools that every visitor must buy

questions.explain: Đoạn 2 kể nguồn gốc ý tưởng và buổi thử nghiệm đầu tiên.

questions.explain: Đoạn 5 nêu các giới hạn nhận đồ và lý do an toàn.

questions.prompt: Why does the repair café use time slots?

To charge visitors for each repair.
To make sure every item is repaired within five minutes.
questions.answer: To help prepare tools and prevent long queues.
questions.explain: Đoạn 3 nói việc đặt giờ giúp chuẩn bị dụng cụ và tránh hàng chờ dài.
